protocol_content.title: Nirsevimab versus placebo for infant RSV prevention
protocol_content.research_question: Among infants no older than one year, compare a single intramuscular dose of nirsevimab with placebo for Review-defined RSV efficacy and safety outcomes.
protocol_content.review_criteria: Include randomized controlled trials of nirsevimab versus placebo in infants no older than one year that report the Review's eligible RSV infection, RSV-related hospitalization, fatal adverse-event or adverse-event-of-special-interest outcomes. Extract participant event counts and arm denominators from eligible full-text reports, appendices or supplementary files.

result_targets.population: Infants no older than one year enrolled in randomized placebo-controlled trials of nirsevimab.
result_targets.outcome: Medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection
result_targets.outcome_definition: Participants with at least one medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection.
result_targets.timepoint: Follow-up reported for the selected Review efficacy outcome.
result_targets.analysis_population: Randomized participants included in the efficacy analysis for the selected outcome.
result_targets.selection_rule: Use directly reported participant event counts and arm denominators for the selected outcome and follow-up.

result_targets.population: Infants no older than one year enrolled in randomized placebo-controlled trials of nirsevimab.
result_targets.outcome: Hospitalization for RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection
result_targets.outcome_definition: Participants hospitalized for an RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection.
result_targets.timepoint: Follow-up reported for the selected Review efficacy outcome.
result_targets.analysis_population: Randomized participants included in the efficacy analysis for the selected outcome.
result_targets.selection_rule: Use directly reported participant event counts and arm denominators for the selected outcome and follow-up.

result_targets.population: Infants no older than one year included in a randomized placebo-controlled trial safety analysis.
result_targets.outcome_definition: Participants with one or more adverse events resulting in death during trial safety follow-up.
result_targets.timepoint: Study-reported safety follow-up corresponding to the Review analysis.
result_targets.analysis_population: Participants included in the study-reported safety analysis for the selected outcome.
result_targets.selection_rule: Use directly reported participant counts for adverse events leading to death and the corresponding arm denominators.

result_targets.population: Infants no older than one year included in a randomized placebo-controlled trial safety analysis.
result_targets.outcome_definition: Participants with hypersensitivity, immune complex disease, or thrombocytopenia, as defined in the Review methods.
result_targets.timepoint: Study-reported safety follow-up corresponding to the Review analysis.
result_targets.analysis_population: Participants included in the study-reported safety analysis for the selected outcome.
result_targets.selection_rule: Use directly reported participant counts for the Review-defined adverse events of special interest and the corresponding arm denominators.

Efficacy of nirsevimab against respiratory syncytial virus lower respiratory tract infections in preterm and term infants: a pooled analysis of randomised controlled trials and pharmacokinetic extrapolation

source_dispositions.detail: The registry remains in the connected Report inventory; the publisher full text supplies the narrower Review-defined safety rows and is the frozen candidate source.
The current registry represents a later All Subjects safety cohort; the publisher full text supplies the Review Primary Cohort safety rows.
The acquired pooled companion is retained for identity and Review cross-checking, but the two primary full texts independently close all four approved targets.
